God's providence is striking here: their efforts to prevent fraud would instead provide evidence that the resurrection was real.
27:64.reflection: How have I seen God work even through the plans of people opposed to Him?
27:64.action: Recall one difficult situation where God brought unexpected good, and share that story with someone today.
27:64.prayer: Sovereign Lord, even sealed stones and armed guards cannot hinder Your purposes. You weave every human plan into Your greater story. Help me trust that nothing can obstruct Your work in my life and in this world. In Christ, amen.

27:65.devotion: Pilate washed his hands of the matter, telling the leaders they had a guard and should secure the tomb as they saw fit. Whether Roman soldiers or temple guards, the authorities did their best to lock death's door. Yet no human security measure could contain what God was about to do on the third day.
27:65.reflection: Where am I relying on human safeguards instead of trusting God's power?
27:65.action: Identify one area where you are over-relying on your own control, and consciously hand it to God in a short prayer today.
27:65.prayer: Father, people sealed the tomb with stone and soldiers, but You hold all power over life and death. Teach me to place my confidence not in earthly safeguards but in Your mighty, resurrecting strength. Through Jesus, amen.

27:66.devotion: The leaders sealed the stone and posted a guard, doing everything within their power to keep the grave shut. The seal marked Roman authority; the watchmen represented human vigilance at its most determined. All of it would become powerless before the angel who came at dawn, underscoring that resurrection was no human scheme.
27:66.reflection: What barriers do I imagine are too firm for God to overcome?
27:66.action: Name one closed door in your life, and ask God today to work in it according to His will.
27:66.prayer: Lord of the open tomb, no seal, stone, or sentinel can restrain Your power. When I face situations that seem locked tight, remind me that nothing is too secure for You to open or too dead for You to raise. Amen.

28:1.devotion: At dawn on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to the tomb. Their devotion is touching: they arrived while it was still dark, bringing loving care for their Lord's body. They expected to mourn; they had no idea they were about to witness the turning point of history.
28:1.reflection: Do I seek Jesus faithfully even when all hope seems buried?
28:1.action: Begin tomorrow, or today if possible, with an early moment devoted to seeking Jesus before other tasks claim your attention.
28:1.prayer: Lord Jesus, the women came to Your tomb while darkness lingered, and dawn met them with resurrection. When my hope feels buried, give me their faithful love to keep seeking You. Meet me in my darkest hours with light. Amen.

28:2.devotion: A great earthquake shook the ground as an angel of the Lord descended, rolled back the stone, and sat upon it. The stone was not removed to let Jesus out—He was already risen—but to let the witnesses in. The angel's resting posture announced calm victory over what once seemed an immovable barrier.
28:2.reflection: What stone of fear or doubt do I need to see rolled away before God's power?
28:2.action: Take a walk or pause outside today and thank God for one specific barrier He has already removed in your life.
28:2.prayer: Almighty God, the earth itself trembled as Your angel rolled away the stone. Remove the stones that block my heart—fear, doubt, and shame—and let me behold the empty tomb with wonder and joy today. In Jesus' risen name, amen.

28:3.devotion: The angel's appearance reflected heaven's glory: his face shone like lightning, and his clothing was white as snow. This dazzling messenger signaled that the events at the tomb were holy and heavenly, not ordinary. The radiance that once excluded sinners from God's presence now announced good news to those who came grieving.
28:3.reflection: How does God's holiness deepen my wonder at the good news of resurrection?
28:3.action: Spend five minutes today reverently praising God for His holiness, perhaps writing down three attributes that fill you with awe.
28:3.prayer: Holy God, Your messenger shone with light too bright for this world, yet he brought good news to grieving hearts. Fill me with reverence for Your holiness and joy that the risen Christ brings me near to You. Amen.

28:4.devotion: At the tomb, the Roman guards who witnessed the angel's descent were overcome with terror and collapsed as though dead. These trained soldiers, meant to secure the grave, were powerless before God's intervention. The scene sets a striking contrast: human strength faints before divine power, while God's saving work unfolds unhindered.
28:4.reflection: Where in my life am I relying on my own strength instead of trusting God's power?
28:4.action: Identify one situation today where you feel powerless, and deliberately pray, entrusting it to God's greater strength.
28:4.prayer: Father, I confess how often I lean on my own strength and fail. Remind me that Your power is greater than every obstacle I face. Help me rest today in Your mighty, unhindered work. Amen.

28:5.devotion: The women came to the tomb grieving, expecting to find a dead body. The angel spoke directly to their hearts: there was no reason to fear. He acknowledged their devotion in seeking Jesus who was crucified. Their faithful love was not overlooked; God met their searching with comfort and astonishing news.
28:5.reflection: What fears might be holding me back from seeking Jesus wholeheartedly right now?
28:5.action: Name one specific fear aloud in prayer today, then take one small step of seeking Jesus through Scripture despite it.
28:5.prayer: Lord Jesus, You see my seeking even when it is tinged with sorrow and fear. Thank You that You never turn away those who look for You. Calm my heart and draw me closer today. Amen.

28:6.devotion: Here stands the heart of the gospel: the tomb is empty because Jesus has risen, exactly as He promised. The angel invites the women to see the evidence for themselves. This is not vague hope but fulfilled promise, confirming that Jesus's words can be trusted fully and death has been defeated.
28:6.reflection: Do I truly believe that Jesus keeps every promise He has made, even the ones still unfulfilled in my life?
28:6.action: Read one promise of Jesus in the Gospels today and write down how it speaks to your current circumstances.
28:6.prayer: Risen Lord, thank You that the empty tomb proves Your word is true. Teach me to trust every promise You have spoken, especially in seasons when I cannot yet see how You will fulfill it. Amen.

28:7.devotion: The women are given a mission: run and tell the disciples that Jesus is alive and is going ahead of them to Galilee. The risen Lord leads His people; He does not linger at the tomb. The angel's closing words reassure them that this message is trustworthy and meant to be shared.
28:7.reflection: Who in my life needs to hear that Jesus is risen and that He goes ahead of those who follow Him?
28:7.action: Share one sentence about the hope of the resurrection with a friend, family member, or coworker today.
28:7.prayer: Jesus, You go before me into every place I will walk this week. Give me courage and readiness to tell others that You are alive, and to invite them to follow where You lead. Amen.

28:8.devotion: The women left the tomb running, filled with both fear and great joy. Their emotions were not tidy; awe and gladness mingled together. Yet they obeyed immediately, hurrying to bring the news to the disciples. Faithful obedience does not require perfect feelings, only willing feet moving toward the task God gives.
28:8.reflection: Am I waiting until my emotions feel settled before I obey what God has placed before me?
28:8.action: Complete one act of obedience you have been postponing, taking the first step today even if you feel hesitant.
28:8.prayer: Father, thank You that You can use me even when my feelings are a mixture of fear and joy. Give me willing feet and a ready heart to carry Your good news to others. Amen.

28:9.devotion: As the women hurried on their mission, Jesus Himself met them with a single word: rejoice. They fell at His feet and worshiped. Before they finished their task, they encountered their risen Lord personally. The good news they carried was not secondhand; they had seen Him and touched the living Savior.
28:9.reflection: When did I last pause to genuinely worship Jesus in the middle of my busy obedience?
28:9.action: Set aside five minutes today to worship Jesus deliberately, perhaps with a song, spoken praise, or silent gratitude.
28:9.prayer: Risen Jesus, meet me in the middle of my ordinary day as You met those faithful women on the road. Receive my worship, and let joy in Your presence strengthen everything I do. Amen.

28:10.devotion: Jesus repeated the angel's command but added a tender phrase: tell My brethren. He calls the disciples who failed and fled His brothers. His first words after rising include reassurance and restoration, not rejection. He invites them to Galilee, where they will see Him, extending grace to those who need it most.
28:10.reflection: Is there someone who has failed me whom Jesus is calling me to view as He views His restored brothers?
28:10.action: Reach out graciously today to someone who has failed or disappointed you, offering a kind word or a fresh start.
28:10.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for calling Your failing followers Your brothers. Thank You that Your first words to the broken were peace, not shame. Help me extend that same restoring grace to others today. Amen.

28:11.devotion: While the women spread joy, the guards reported the astonishing events to the chief priests. Matthew shows two responses to the same evidence: some move toward faith and proclamation, others toward damage control. The empty tomb demands a response from everyone who hears of it. Indifference is never truly an option.
28:11.reflection: How am I responding to the reality of the resurrection, honestly or with convenient avoidance?
28:11.action: Examine one area where you have resisted a truth about Jesus, and honestly bring it to Him in prayer today.
28:11.prayer: Father, the news of the risen Christ demands a response from me. Forgive me for the times I have softened or avoided Your truth. Give me an honest heart that responds to Jesus with faith and obedience. Amen.

28:12.devotion: After Jesus rose from the dead, the guards reported the astonishing events to the chief priests. Rather than rejoicing or investigating honestly, the religious leaders gathered with the elders and plotted together, choosing to pay a bribe to suppress the truth of the resurrection they had just heard about.
28:12.reflection: Have I ever resisted evidence that God was at work because it would upset my plans or reputation?
28:12.action: Identify one truth from Scripture you have been avoiding or explaining away, and bring it honestly to God in prayer today.
28:12.prayer: Lord, keep my heart soft toward Your truth. Where fear, pride, or convenience makes me resistant to what You are doing, forgive me and give me courage to respond honestly to You. In Jesus' name, Amen.

28:13.devotion: The authorities instructed the soldiers to spread a story: that the disciples stole Jesus' body while they slept. The explanation was implausible on its face, yet it shows how far people will go to avoid facing the risen Christ. The lie replaced the truth they did not want to believe.
28:13.reflection: When confronted with something that demands a response, do I turn toward truth or toward convenient explanations?
28:13.action: Examine one area where you have preferred a comfortable story over God's truth, and write down what honesty would look like instead.
28:13.prayer: Father, guard me from self-deception. Give me a love for truth that is stronger than my love for comfort, so that I may face Your Son honestly and follow Him faithfully. Amen.

28:14.devotion: The elders promised to protect the soldiers if the false report reached the governor, since sleeping on duty was a serious offense. Their pledge reveals the depth of the conspiracy: money, influence, and cover-ups joined together to silence the news of the resurrection.
28:14.reflection: Am I willing to trust God with the consequences of telling the truth, even when it costs me?
28:14.action: Choose one situation today where honesty might be inconvenient, and speak truthfully in it, trusting God with the outcome.
28:14.prayer: Lord, it is tempting to protect myself with half-truths. Help me to trust You with the cost of honesty, knowing You see all things and care for those who walk in integrity. In Christ's name, Amen.

28:15.devotion: The soldiers took the money and repeated the story, and Matthew notes that this saying circulated widely among the Jews even to his day. A lie told long enough can seem settled history. Yet Matthew's Gospel itself stands as testimony that the authorities' story could not erase what actually happened.
28:15.reflection: What voices or reports am I accepting without examining them in light of God's word?
28:15.action: Take one rumor, complaint, or claim you heard recently and test it against Scripture before repeating or believing it.
28:15.prayer: Father, in a world full of competing stories, anchor me in Your word. Give me discernment to recognize falsehood and confidence in the truth of the risen Christ. Amen.

28:16.devotion: The eleven remaining disciples obeyed Jesus' prior instruction and traveled to Galilee, to the mountain He had appointed. Their obedience brought them to the place of encounter. The risen Lord met them exactly where He had promised, on ground He Himself had chosen for this momentous meeting.
28:16.reflection: Where is Jesus calling me to go or to meet Him, and am I obeying?
28:16.action: Complete one act of obedience you know Jesus has asked of you, even if it feels ordinary or unclear.
28:16.prayer: Lord Jesus, You appoint the places and times of encounter. Give me grace to obey Your instructions promptly, trusting that obedience leads me into Your presence. Amen.

28:17.devotion: Seeing the risen Jesus, the disciples worshiped Him, yet Matthew honestly records that some doubted. Even in the presence of the risen Christ, faith and uncertainty mingled. Scripture does not hide the disciples' struggle; it shows that Jesus receives worshipers who are also wrestling with questions.
28:17.reflection: Where does doubt still linger in my worship, and can I bring it honestly to Jesus?
28:17.action: Name one doubt or question you carry about faith, and share it honestly with God or with a mature believer today.
28:17.prayer: Lord Jesus, You welcome even my half-held faith. Meet me in my doubts as You met Your disciples, and steady my heart until my worship is whole. Amen.

28:18.devotion: Jesus responded to their worship and doubt with a sweeping declaration: all authority in heaven and on earth has been given to Him. Before commissioning His disciples, He grounds the mission in His own supreme authority. The risen Christ reigns over everything, which makes His command trustworthy and His presence reliable.
28:18.reflection: Do I live today as though Jesus truly holds all authority over my life, work, and future?
28:18.action: Surrender one specific decision or worry to Jesus today, consciously acknowledging His authority over it in prayer.
28:18.prayer: Lord Jesus, all authority in heaven and on earth is Yours. Rule over my plans, my fears, and my tomorrows. Teach me to rest under Your gracious reign. Amen.

28:19.devotion: Because He holds all authority, Jesus commands His followers to go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. The mission flows from His reign. Every follower of Jesus is drawn into sharing His good news and helping others become His students.
28:19.reflection: Whom has God placed in my life who needs to hear about Jesus and be invited to follow Him?
28:19.action: Reach out today to one person who does not know Jesus, through a conversation, an invitation, or a prayerful message.
28:19.prayer: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, send me into Your world as Your witness. Give me boldness, gentleness, and love to make disciples who follow Jesus all their days. Amen.

28:20.devotion: At the close of Matthew's Gospel, the risen Jesus commissions His disciples to teach others to obey all He has commanded. Alongside that great task stands a great promise: His presence accompanies them always, until the end of the age. Obedience and mission are never carried out alone.
28:20.reflection: Where in my life do I need to remember today that Jesus is with me?
28:20.action: Choose one task or conversation that feels daunting today, and consciously invite Jesus' presence into it before you begin.
28:20.prayer: Lord Jesus, thank You for the promise of Your constant presence. Help me live obediently and share Your word boldly, knowing You walk with me every step until the end of the age. Amen.
